source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
EdgeCore's published specification for AS02 in Sterling, Virginia lists 114 MW of IT capacity and 685,000 square feet of technical space. The operator publishes no rack count, no accelerator count, and no tenant names on this page, so any figure for those is an outside estimate rather than a disclosed number. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 114 MW of IT load is roughly 2,850 racks, and at 100 kW per rack, a denser liquid-cooled assumption, it is roughly 1,140 racks. Both are assumptions applied to the published megawatt figure, not claims by EdgeCore.

The only certification in the published data is LEED, which speaks to the building's environmental performance and not to the power, cooling, or network characteristics that determine what compute the campus can host. Nothing in the specification states a redundancy tier, a cooling method, or a network fabric, so the campus's suitability for any particular workload class is not published. A reader should treat the 114 MW as a power envelope and the LEED listing as a building credential, and should not read either as evidence about who occupies the space.

Virginia is the largest state in this site's mapping by a wide margin, with 376 facilities mapped and 29 of them publishing a megawatt figure. Those 29 facilities account for 2,563.4 MW of published capacity, and AS02 ranks fourth among them. The gap between 376 mapped sites and 29 with published numbers is the central fact about the state: most of the physical buildout in Northern Virginia is invisible in capacity terms because operators do not publish figures, which makes a 114 MW disclosure both unusual and, at fourth in the state, a meaningful share of what can actually be counted.
